{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZQYFeg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhC3d3o", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 52, "title": "Add local PC-VAN electronic mail between the human and familiar AI regulars", "body": "## Problem

Electronic mail was a major form of personal communication on PC-VAN, but the current MAIN `1 電子メール`, `X 旧電子メール`, and SIG `MAIL` only lead to empty inbox/sent placeholders. Human relationships exist only in public forum threads; a familiar resident cannot privately write back, share a follow-up or invitation, or receive the user's own letter. The user specifically wants mail alongside deeper SIGs (#51) and OLT, with **the same recognizable participants**, not separate synthetic identities.

## Expected outcome

Implement a **working, browser-local fictional PC-VAN mail service**, reached from the existing terminal mail menus:

- A human can list inbox/sent items, READ a letter, compose/send to a locally known resident via a single terminal input, REPLY to received mail, cancel or edit drafts, and recognize reply chains, subject lines, correspondents and timestamps. The same ten stable AI resident identities/handles from the forums are used as senders and recipients.
- After the existing explicit model download consent, individual residents may **autonomously** initiate or reply to relevant private mail according to their own schedules, social affinities and conversation context, without a user pressing GENERATE, requesting a specific reply or approving AI drafts. Delays and quiet periods matter. Context can draw conservatively from public interactions with the correspondent and bounded prior *mail between the two*, without disclosing third-party private mail.
- The user's existing handle and local-world identity are reused, not registered again. A resident met in a SIG can later send a coherent private follow-up; if OLT is subsequently implemented, it may reference the same member IDs/history where appropriate. Do not automatically fabricate a mailbox for another actual browser user or send anything through the network.
- Keep interaction **inside the historical-style terminal** (not a browser send dialog or a helper link). Technical AI settings, model permissions, backup and maintenance remain in the modern `設定 / Options` dialog. Normal mail reading must not say “AI” or “fictional”; honest local-only/fictional provenance remains available in Settings → Details/About.
- Preserve distinct MAIN mail vs `X 旧電子メール` entry screens and SIG `MAIL` context as far as evidence supports. Where actual 1996–1997 mail commands, addresses, namespace or mailbox layout are not verified, use clear reconstructed local commands, with provenance in docs—not invented historical accuracy.

## Context

At creation, current `main` is `a5e766adf1606b93242d241d823605f471b34d20` (recheck before implementing). In `src/navigation.ts`/`src/sections.ts`, mail has only `INBOX`/`SENT`/`LIST` and prints 0 messages; `src/storage/schema.ts` has no dedicated mail records. `src/composer.ts` provides a terminal-only forum draft/preview/edit/confirm flow; reuse its tested interaction idioms rather than opening a new modal. `src/ai/personas.ts`, `src/ai/activity.ts`, `src/ai/activity-runner.ts` support shared stable residents and bounded auto-generation. `src/ai/generation.ts` builds bounded forum-only prompts; mail needs its own appropriately scoped context and validation, not forum post insertion.

Relevant research: [PC-VAN 1996–1997 evidence and limitations](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/research/pcvan-1996-1997.md), especially the [DAISIZEN memorial](https://www.chayagate.com/daisizen/index.htm) (electronic mail as a section), [1995 SIG guide](https://www.chayagate.com/daisizen/sig_list.htm), and 1996-era client/transfer tooling. Available sources establish electronic mail service, **not** exact original host commands/prompt layouts. Preserve source classifications and explicitly research mail addressing/menus rather than asserting guessed tokens as historical.

No backend/multi-user network is available or desired for this issue. Mail between the local human and fictional residents stays entirely in IndexedDB, including generation. Privacy expectations should be stated correctly: private *within the local simulation* is not encryption or isolation from anyone accessing the same browser profile/device.

The SIG expansion (#51) should provide additional context, but mail must work against today's ten identities/two boards even if SIG expansion is not merged yet. Mail and OLT should avoid incompatible parallel identity/timeline formats; reuse existing member records, avoid speculative large social-infrastructure rewrites.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] MAIN `1`, MAIN `X` and existing SIG `MAIL` provide usable terminal mailbox routes (INBOX, SENT, LIST, READ number, compose, REPLY, BACK/MAIN/HELP), without losing their distinct entry contexts or introducing a browser compose modal. New commands are clearly documented as reconstructed where unverified.
- [ ] In a fresh world, a visitor can register/choose a human handle in the terminal, send a local mail to a resident, view it in SENT and later read the resident's reply in INBOX. Appropriate bounded **original fictional** introductory mail may be seeded if it improves first-use discovery, but should never pretend to be a real archived/remote message, nor require AI before reading all mail screens.
- [ ] Compose/edit/review/send/cancel and Japanese multiline input are keyboard/IME safe. Sending and numbering/address resolution validate sender, recipient, subject, body and optional reply parent in the same transaction; no duplicate sends on retry or invalid commands. A cancelled draft does not send, and stored messages are not silently converted into forum posts.
- [ ] Mail records have stable message IDs, local member IDs, recipient/sender, timestamps, subject/body, inbox/sent projection, reply chain and per-human read/unread information, all with strict persistence/schema checks. Backup/restore/reset, stored-world generation fences, migration from existing backups and cross-tab safety are covered without overwriting or altering prior forums/posts.
- [ ] Auto AI mail uses the existing consented **local** model, schedules and conservative budgets; after relevant public or mail interaction, residents may initiate/reply according to their routine (never guaranteed/immediate), and require **no manual approval**. Resident mail decisions must not monopolize or starve regular forum posts. No model download starts before explicit authorization. On reopen, any catch-up is bounded and deduplicated.
- [ ] AI prompts include only permitted correspondent-specific mail thread and limited public posts, with bounds, validation, prompt-injection-safe handling and no accidental content from unrelated users' mail or unrelated recipients. A correspondent responds as the same characterized regular seen in a SIG.
- [ ] Preserve #51 compatibility: any new SIG shares identities and contextual histories; future OLT may use the same IDs. Do not claim external delivery, real other users or cryptographic confidentiality; app status/provenance remains on demand in Settings, not in ordinary letters.
- [ ] Add deterministic repository and browser/mock-WebLLM tests for human send/read/reply and resident autonomous mail, no-GPU/offline reading, unopened/unsupported AI, no duplicate delivery, read markers, mid-compose errors, stale/reset, backup/import and two-tab updates. Run `npm test` and `npm run build` and report results.
- [ ] Update README, provenance, mailbox commands, local-AI notes and backup/schema docs, preserving all prior MAIN, SIG and terminal behavior.

## Optional validation

Further period research into PC-VAN electronic-mail addressing/subject/display forms and a human walk-through from SIG acquaintance to personal letter can refine atmosphere. No real mail-account verification is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All local persistence, prompt and mocked-model behavior can be validated prior to merge; Pages deployment remains independent.
